name: MOLLER
notes: Status as of 2026-10-26 from the collaboration talks and the JLab Hall A February 2026 update: installation in progress, running planned from 2027 for three years (earlier targets of 2025/2026 slipped).
DOE project milestones (CD-2/CD-3) were not found in any fetched source; the funding line "DOE (MIE), NSF, CFI/RM" is from the APS 2025 talk.

Target length differs between sources (1.5 m in the proposal text on moller.jlab.org, 1.25 m on the 2025 status slide) and the precision goal differs (0.7 ppb versus 0.8 ppb), so neither is recorded as a spec.

physics_goals.quote: proposes to measure the parity-violating asymmetry in electron-electron (Møller) scattering
physics_goals.value: Measure the parity-violating asymmetry in electron-electron (Møller) scattering to determine the weak charge of the electron and the weak mixing angle at low Q^2

summary.plain: MOLLER, now being installed at Jefferson Lab, will measure the tiny difference in how left- and right-spinning electrons scatter off other electrons. That reveals the electron's weak charge, a precision test of the Standard Model sensitive to new physics at multi-TeV mass scales.
summary.technical: Measurement Of a Lepton-Lepton Electroweak Reaction: parity-violating asymmetry A_PV (about 33 ppb predicted) in Møller scattering of an 11 GeV longitudinally polarised electron beam on a liquid-hydrogen target in Hall A, with a toroidal-magnet spectrometer and fused-silica Cherenkov detectors, aiming at a sub-ppb measurement of the electron weak charge and of sin^2(theta_W) at Q^2 = 0.0056 GeV^2; installation in Hall A in progress, physics running planned from 2027.
